name: Eccentric Reverse Lunge
instructions: Stand tall, then step one foot straight back into a reverse lunge.
Lower over a slow 3-4 count until both knees approach 90 degrees.
Drive through the front heel to return to standing — the way up is normal speed.
Alternate legs. The slow lowering builds single-leg strength and control.
longevityNotes: Single-leg strength is balance insurance — the ability to catch yourself on one leg prevents falls. Train lunges for control, not maximal load.
overview: A beginner bodyweight lunge-pattern exercise targeting the quadriceps. Eccentric Reverse Lunge develops single-leg strength and stability that transfers to walking, stairs, and sport.
